## 2) What’s in your *own* legal annex that points to **alternatives the Judge could/should have considered**

Your **Annex B – Legal Authorities & Framework** flags these guardrails:

- **Rule 38 (Strike-out)** is “draconian”; the Tribunal **must consider proportionality and alternatives**. fileciteturn40file0L13-L16  
- **Rule 39 (Deposit Orders)** require “**little reasonable prospect**” and **means** assessment (she did include means). fileciteturn40file0L17-L19  
- **Blockbuster v James**: strike-out sparingly; last-minute tactics undermine fairness. fileciteturn40file0L29-L33  
- **Cox v Adecco**: don’t strike out where facts are disputed or **lesser sanctions** suffice. fileciteturn40file0L33-L35  
- **Harris v AET**: case management must be **even-handed**; excusing one side while penalising the other engages **Rule 3**. fileciteturn40file0L31-L33

You also **asked for an Unless Order** in your 9–16 Sept emails: an order compelling a compliant disability response within 7 days **failing which** the Respondent would be barred from contesting disability—i.e., **a proportionate alternative**. fileciteturn40file14L31-L37 fileciteturn40file14L56-L58

**My read:** your papers squarely raised **proportionality** and **Unless Orders** as alternatives to punitive outcomes; the PH Order’s reasoning records deposit and disability outcomes but (from the document) doesn’t explicitly grapple with **why an Unless Order was rejected** in light of your Rule-31/38/40 correspondence.

## 3) **Peninsula v Baker**—how your uploads frame it

Your “Peninsula” analyses stress two transferable points:

- **Victimisation (s.27)** requires strict **“because of”** causation and employer **knowledge** of the **specific protected act**—no vague triggers. fileciteturn40file2L37-L43 fileciteturn40file8L1-L7

- **Disability harassment/claims**: **actual disability** generally required; otherwise the route is **victimisation** for detriments following a protected act (complaint/appeal). fileciteturn40file2L29-L35

Applied to your case: the Judge’s **Deposit reasons** say you didn’t link detriments **because of** the protected characteristics, and that you **raised the discrimination** only **after** the process began. fileciteturn40file5L11-L17 That’s where the **Peninsula** line of argument (strict causation + knowledge of *which* protected act) becomes the battlefield for victimisation and comparators. Your uploads argue that your **appeal** and internal complaints were **protected acts** known to named managers. fileciteturn40file8L5-L11

# 1) Judge’s test for strike-out (ET Rules 2013, r.37) — where this really sits

* **Rule 37**: strike-out is only where a claim (or part) has **no reasonable prospect of success**.
* **Discrimination claims** are rarely suitable for strike-out: they usually require **fact-finding** and often **medical evidence**. A Rule 37 decision **is not** a mini-trial on disputed facts or medical causation.
* Practical judicial lens:

  * If there’s **any real factual dispute** (e.g., onset/recurrence; employer **knowledge** on/before **6 Aug 2024**; what adjustments were **available**; whether decisions were **because of** protected acts/traits), strike-out is **not appropriate**.
  * The proportionate course is a **preliminary issue** (e.g., disability) with **directions for medical evidence**, not strike-out.

**Ask the Judge now:** “Even if the current medical material is thin, the proper case management is a **preliminary issue on disability**, not Rule 37 strike-out.”

# 2) Disability in law (EqA 2010, s.6 & Schedule 1) — why ‘stress caused by discipline’ is the wrong test

* **Legal test**: a **mental impairment** with a **substantial** and **long-term** adverse effect on **normal day-to-day activities**.
* **Cause is not disqualifying**: It **doesn’t matter why** the impairment arose (work events, disciplinary, personal). The question is **what effects** it had and whether they were **substantial** and **long-term** (or **likely** to last 12 months / **likely** to **recur**).
* **Episodic/recurring conditions** (anxiety/depression) still qualify if effects are substantial and **likely to recur** (Schedule 1).
* **Timing**: assess “long-term” based on what was **known or could reasonably be expected** at the material time — not with hindsight only.

**So even if** symptoms intensified around the disciplinary, that **does not bar** disability. The question is: do your **MHIS + GP records** show **substantial** effects and **duration/likelihood**?

---

# 3) s.15 EqA (discrimination arising from disability) — why this still bites

* **Causation**: treatment “**arising in consequence of**” disability is a **loose causal link** (it need **not** be the only or main cause).
* **Knowledge**: the employer’s **knowledge of disability** is a **separate limb**; your **1 Aug 2024 MED3** and the **6 Aug** email acknowledgement are potent on this.

> **(1)** The Tribunal must consider any application made under rule 69 (application for reconsideration).  
> **(2)** If the Tribunal considers that there is no reasonable prospect of the judgment being varied or revoked (including, unless there are special reasons, where substantially the same application has already been made and refused), the application must be refused and the Tribunal must inform the parties of the refusal.  
> **(3)** If the application has not been refused under paragraph (2), the Tribunal must send a notice to the parties specifying the period by which any written representations in respect of the application must be received by the Tribunal, and seeking the views of the parties on whether the application can be determined without a hearing. The notice may also set out the Tribunal’s provisional views on the application.  
> **(4)** If the application has not been refused under paragraph (2), the judgment must be reconsidered at a hearing unless the Tribunal considers, having regard to any written representations provided under paragraph (3), that a hearing is not necessary in the interests of justice.

Just to male sure, we applied and following below yea ? ased on the UK's Employment Tribunals Rules of Procedure 2013, an Application for Reconsideration under Rule 70 is a request for a tribunal to review and potentially change its own judgment. The tribunal's decision can be confirmed, varied, or revoked, and if it is revoked, the case may be reheard. 

Principles of reconsideration (Rule 70)
	•	"Interests of justice": A tribunal can reconsider a judgment "where it is necessary in the interests of justice to do so". It is not enough to simply disagree with the outcome. The grounds for reconsideration often involve issues like:
	◦	New evidence: Where new evidence has been discovered that could not reasonably have been known or foreseen at the time of the hearing.
	◦	Procedural irregularity: A significant mistake was made in the tribunal's procedure.
	◦	Obvious mistake: An obvious error was made in the judgment, such as a miscalculation.
	•	Time limit: An application must be submitted in writing within 14 days of the date the written judgment or reasons for it were sent. The tribunal may grant an extension for a compelling reason.
	•	Initial review: An Employment Judge first reviews the application. If they believe there is no reasonable prospect of the original decision being varied or revoked, the application will be refused without a hearing.
	•	Reconsideration hearing: If the initial review is successful, the tribunal will seek views from the other parties. A reconsideration hearing will be held unless the judge believes it is unnecessary in the interests of justice.
	•	Who handles it?: Reconsideration is typically handled by the same judge or panel that made the original decision, if practicable. 

Reconsideration vs. appeal
It is crucial to understand the difference between a reconsideration and an appeal. 

Aspect 
Reconsideration (Rule 70)
Appeal (to Employment Appeal Tribunal)
Venue
The same Employment Tribunal that made the original decision.
The Employment Appeal Tribunal (EAT), a higher court.
Grounds
"Interests of justice." This covers mistakes of fact, procedural errors, and new evidence.
"Error of law" only, such as misapplying the law or a perverse conclusion that no reasonable tribunal could have reached.
Purpose
To ask the tribunal to fix an issue internally before escalating the case.
To challenge a decision on a point of law in a higher court.
Effect on time limits
Applying for reconsideration does not extend the time limit for an appeal. The 42-day appeal deadline runs from when the written reasons for the original judgment were sent.
N/A

What to do if you are challenging a decision
	1	Request written reasons. If the judgment does not include written reasons, you should request them from the tribunal within 14 days.
	2	Decide between reconsideration and appeal. You can pursue both at the same time, but it is important to be mindful of the different deadlines and grounds. Some legal practitioners advise against reconsideration if you plan to appeal, as it can be used by the tribunal to strengthen its initial decision.
	3	Prepare your application. If you proceed with a reconsideration, you must write to the tribunal, explaining why it is necessary in the interests of justice. If you are citing new evidence, you must explain why it was unavailable earlier.
	4	Lodge the appeal. If you decide to appeal, you must file with the EAT within 42 days of the date the written reasons for the judgment were sent.

# What “reasonably be expected to know” means (in law)

- **Statute:** The duty to make reasonable adjustments arises where the employer **knows, or could reasonably be expected to know**, that a worker **is disabled** and **is, or is likely to be, placed at a substantial disadvantage** by a PCP (e.g., insisting on attending a disciplinary while unfit). This knowledge requirement is set out in **Schedule 8 to the Equality Act 2010** (read with ss.20–21). citeturn0search5turn0search0

- **EHRC Employment Code (statutory guidance):** Employers must make adjustments when they **know or could reasonably be expected to know**; they should take **reasonable steps to find out** if support is needed—i.e., not turn a blind eye to signs of difficulty. (Tribunals may take this Code into account.) citeturn0search1turn0search6

- **Case law guard-rails:**
  - **Gallop v Newport CC (CA):** Employers **cannot outsource the judgment** about disability—don’t rely uncritically on OH; form your **own** view from the info available. citeturn0search2
  - **Donelien v Liberata (CA):** If an employer **does** take **reasonable investigative steps** (e.g., referrals, clarifying questions) but still can’t tell, it **may not** have constructive knowledge. The test is reasonableness of the employer’s enquiries. citeturn0search8turn0search13

I believe the process and decision were not conducted in accordance with ACAS guidelines and the Co-op disciplinary procedures. I would like to highlight several concerns and request a fair review of my case. *Lack of Transparency and Fairness* *Investigation Meeting (29.07.2024):* I was asked to attend the office without prior notice or an understanding of the reason, causing significant stress and anxiety. This unexpected approach severely impacted my mental well-being, affecting my ability to clearly express my side of the story during the meeting. Additionally, there was no neutral note-taker present, with notes being taken solely by Pankaj Patel. This raises concerns about the impartiality and accuracy of the documentation. The decision to suspend me was made within two hours, without a thorough investigation or any informal discussion, which does not align with ACAS guidelines recommending that all other options be considered before suspension. *Disciplinary Meeting Scheduled (01.08.2024):* There was no attempt to resolve the issue informally before moving to formal disciplinary action. The stress and anxiety caused by the sudden escalation to formal proceedings further impacted my mental well-being, diminishing my capacity to fully articulate my perspective. ACAS guidelines emphasize the importance of informal discussions to fully understand the issue, yet this step was bypassed in my case. Furthermore, I was not informed of my right to be accompanied by a colleagu= e or trade union representative during the disciplinary meeting, as outlined in the ACAS guidelines. This oversight further exacerbated my stress and limited my ability to effectively present my case. It is also important to note that this is not the first time I have experienced such rushed disciplinary procedures. Approximately one month ago, I was invited to another disciplinary meeting, which similarly resulted in a written warning without any informal discussion. This pattern of rushing through disciplinary processes without the opportunity for informal resolution or thorough investigation suggests a disregard for the principles of fairness and transparency as outlined by ACAS and Co-op guidelines. *Health and Well-being Considerations* *Health Condition and Communication (05.08.2024):* I informed my team about my health condition and provided a sick note. Despite this, the disciplinary meeting was scheduled without consideration of my health and well-being, contrary to ACAS guidelines, which stress the importance of considering an employee=E2=80=99s health during disciplinary processes. *Bias and Pre-judgment* *Disciplinary Meeting and Outcome (12.08.2024):* Despite my health condition, I attended the meeting to demonstrate my commitment. However, the stress and anxiety from the entire process significantly affected my mental state, making it difficult for me to effectively communicate my side of the story. This is evident in the outcome documentation, where my statement about not smoking but unintentionally taking a puff was omitted. This omission suggests a lack of thorough consideration of my account, further exacerbating my concerns about bias and pre-judgment in the process. I am also concerned about potential inconsistencies in the application of the Co-op=E2=80=99s disciplinary procedures. From what I understand, other employees in similar situations have received different treatment, raising concerns about fairness and consistency in how these policies are applied. *Monitoring and Privacy Concerns* *Excessive and Unnecessary Monitoring:* Pankaj Patel mentioned that the incident came to his attention while he was not in the building, implying I was monitored through cameras. This level of monitoring was excessive and unnecessary, violating my privacy. According to ACAS guidelines, employers must inform employees about any monitoring arrangements and the reasons for them. This was not done in my case, constituting a violation of my privacy rights and damaging trust. *Inaccurate Documentation and Lack of Thorough Investigation* *Discrepancies in Investigation Notes:* The investigation notes inaccurately state that I opened the package and put it in a bag. In reality, I found the package already opened and was unaware of its contents. Additionally, another team leader, Gorin, knew exactly what was in the package, which raises questions about how he obtained this information. This aspect was neither investigated nor addressed. Moreover, I was not given sufficient time to respond to the evidence presented against me. The lack of detailed information and the rushed nature of the investigation process made it difficult for me to prepare a thorough defence, as recommended by ACAS guidelines. *Misrepresentation of the Smoking Incident* *Misleading Outcome Documentation:* During the investigation meeting, I clearly stated that I did not smoke but unintentionally took a puff while reading a document during my break. The outcome documentation, however, misleadingly suggests that I was smoking in the building, which does not accurately reflect the events. *Impact on Work Performance* The stress and anxiety caused by the disciplinary process have significantly impacted my ability to perform my duties effectively. This should be taken into consideration as per the ACAS guidelines, which stress the importance of supporting employee well-being during such processes. *Request for Fair Review* In light of these points, I respectfully request a fair review of the disciplinary process and outcome. I believe the process was not conducted in line with the principles of fairness and transparency as outlined by ACAS and the Co-op disciplinary procedures. I request a more balanced and thorough investigation into the matter. Thank you for your attention to this appeal. I look forward to your response and a fair resolution. | **(C) “No earlier records matching MHIS symptoms before Aug-2024” (para 14)** | MHIS says symptoms began Oct-2023 and escalated by Jan-2024. fileciteturn39file3L17-L19 | We’ve not found GP records **before Aug-2024** in your upload. Your **first NHS entries** are Aug 2024 (fit note, GP contacts), then Sep 2024 (scores/notes). fileciteturn39file13L83-L97 | The Judge is correct **on the documentary record**: there’s no **pre-Aug-2024** GP evidence in the bundle. | **(D) Long-term (“could well happen”) at **the date** (Aug-2024)** | MHIS shows a **long trajectory**: GAD-7/PHQ-9 on **9 Sep 2024**; **propranolol from Dec 2024**; ongoing therapy (UK/Turkey); psychiatrist **unfit to work Feb 2025**. fileciteturn39file2L16-L19 fileciteturn39file8L3-L11 | Evidence of **persistence** is strong **after** Aug-2024 (Sept 2024 onwards). The NHS app also documents Aug–Sep progression. fileciteturn39file13L68-L81 | Judge applied **Boyle**/**McDougall** (assess **as at** Aug-2024). Your materials show persistence, but the **prognosis at the time** (Aug-2024) isn’t explicitly stated by a clinician in the records we saw. |

thoughts.content: I’m thinking the best approach is to offer strategies that are empathetic yet firm. For instance, using a "Mischaracterization Correction Note" to outline the quote, correction, evidence, and why it matters. I’d also recommend a neutral, precise tone, focusing on correcting "inaccuracies" instead of accusing “dishonesty.” A timeline highlighting misstatements works too.

The instructions say I need citations or a navlist if using specific sources or tools. However, I think I can avoid citations if I keep the response general. It seems I haven’t used any file sources in this turn, but I could always follow up later with citations if needed for accuracy.

The user asked for advice on expressing a mischaracterization, like the "after 6 o'clock submission" issue. Instead of directly quoting the text from a prior order, I’ll suggest crafting a "Mischaracterization Corrections" document. It could include a template with sections for tone, law, and specific corrections like the “after 6pm” example.

Entering JUDGE_MODE. Here’s a focused procedural assessment on: (A) compliance with the Case Management Order (“CMO”) made at the Preliminary Hearing on 3 June 2025—specifically paragraph 7—and (B) disclosure under Rule 31 ET Rules 2013.

# Findings

## A) CMO (03-Jun-2025) — Paragraph 7 (disability stance by 12 Aug 2025)

**What para 7 required (as evidenced in party correspondence):**  
Respondent to confirm whether it accepts the Claimant had a disability, and if so on what dates, **by 12 August 2025**. This requirement is explicitly referenced by the Claimant when asking the Tribunal to confirm whether any response was received, and noting that **CMO paragraph 14** requires all correspondence to be **copied to both parties**. 【50:0†Source.file†L24-L33】【50:0†Source.file†L44-L46】

**Compliance status (on the face of the file):**  
- **Respondent:** As of **13 August 2025**, the Claimant reports **no receipt** of any response satisfying para 7, and asks the Tribunal to confirm if anything was filed directly with it. On the evidence available, this suggests **non-compliance** or **service to Tribunal only (not copied)** contrary to para 14. 【50:0†Source.file†L30-L36】【50:0†Source.file†L38-L46】  
- **Tribunal copy requirement (para 14):** If the Respondent did file with the Tribunal but failed to copy the Claimant, that would be a **breach of para 14** of the same CMO. 【50:0†Source.file†L44-L46】

**Conclusion on para 7:**  
On the available record, **Respondent appears not to have complied by 12 August 2025**, or at least failed to copy the Claimant as required. Confirmation from the Tribunal registry was expressly requested by the Claimant the next day. 【50:0†Source.file†L30-L36】【50:0†Source.file†L38-L46】

---

## B) Rule 31 — Disclosure/inspection orders & CMO schedule

**CMO disclosure timetable captured in the case file:**  
- **18 June 2025:** Claimant to disclose relevant documents to Respondent (and related preparation milestones). 【50:1†Source.file†L1-L4】  
- **25 June 2025:** Parties to agree bundle contents (not Rule 31 itself, but part of case preparation ordered at PH). 【50:1†Source.file†L3-L3】

**Compliance shown in the file:**  
- **Claimant:** Emailed **“Final Disclosure List”** on **18 June 2025**, acknowledging it was filed **slightly late on the day** due to a health episode but confirming it was submitted and served the same day. This is **substantial compliance** with the Rule 31 disclosure timetable set in the 3 June CMO. 【39†turn0file16†L1-L9】【39†turn0file16†L17-L25】  
- **Respondent:** No clear evidence in the uploaded set demonstrating **their** compliance with any reciprocal Rule 31 disclosure obligation by the same schedule. (Status **unknown** on current record.)

**Context in the materials:**  
Previous analysis notes flag the 18 June disclosure date as a CMO requirement and record the Claimant’s “compliant filing” on that date. 【50:6†Source.file†L28-L33】【50:14†Source.file†L1-L4】

**Conclusion on Rule 31:**  
- **Claimant:** **Complied** (minor same-day lateness explained; documents served). 【39†turn0file16†L1-L9】【39†turn0file16†L17-L25】  
- **Respondent:** **Not evidenced** in these files—no affirmative proof of timely disclosure under the CMO’s Rule 31 schedule.

---

# Summary (for the Judge’s note)

- **CMO (03-Jun-2025) para 7:** On the documents provided, **Respondent appears non-compliant** with the 12 Aug 2025 deadline (and/or failed to copy per para 14). Tribunal confirmation was requested by Claimant on **13 Aug 2025**. 【50:0†Source.file†L24-L33】【50:0†Source.file†L44-L46】  
- **Rule 31 disclosure:** **Claimant complied** on 18 Jun 2025 (minor same-day delay explained; served). **Respondent’s position remains unproven** on this record. 【39†turn0file16†L1-L9】【39†turn0file16†L17-L25】【50:1†Source.file†L1-L4】

parts:
You’re right: **para 11’s wording is ambiguous**. It does two different things in one sentence:

1) **Acknowledges** you supplied an impact statement (“He had supplied an impact statement…”), and  
2) **Explains weight**, not receipt (“…however that was not supported by the medical records.”)

So, read strictly, the judge is saying: *“I had it, but I’m giving it little weight because I can’t see corroborating medical entries around the material time.”* It isn’t stating (or denying) whether she read every page—just that she didn’t find **medical** support for it.

If you want the record to be crystal clear, here’s a tight, judge-friendly clarification you can drop into a short note (no argument, just accuracy):

### Micro-clarification (for the record)
> **Para 11 – Impact statement: receipt vs weight**  
> The Tribunal records that I “supplied an impact statement.” For accuracy, please confirm that the impact statement was **received and considered**, and that the Tribunal’s comment concerns **weight** (lack of contemporaneous **medical** corroboration), rather than any suggestion it was not read.  
> For ease of reference, contemporaneous items on file include: **fit notes (1–15 Aug and 15–30 Aug 2024)** and **GP entries on 19 Aug / 9 Sep**.

If you prefer a one-line gloss you can place in your bundle:

> **How to read para 11:** “Impact statement provided ✔︎; Tribunal gave it low **weight** due to limited **medical** corroboration for August 2024.”

If you want, I’ll add a tiny side-box in the matrix/chronology that shows:
- **Impact statement → considered** (para 11 first clause)  
- **Why discounted → lack of contemporaneous medical D2D entries** (para 11/16)  
- **Your Aug items → fit notes + 19 Aug/9 Sep entries** (so a reader sees what exists).

You’re right: the **operative CMO** is the one **dated 3 June 2025 (served 8 June)**, and you **complied** with it by filing your **trimmed/final Disclosure List on 18 June 2025 at 01:07**. That’s clear on the face of your email and the list itself (prepared “pursuant to Case Management Orders dated 3 June 2025”). fileciteturn58file1 fileciteturn58file2

The PH Order’s para 25 only mentions your **9 April** disclosure application. If the Judge then assessed “relevance” while overlooking your later **CMO-compliant 18 June** list, that’s a **material misapprehension of the procedural record** (good ground for reconsideration).

I tried to drop a new “Ground 6” into your **Rule 70 Reconsideration – Draft (Merged with Knowledge Matrix)** on the canvas, but the auto-insertion failed because the heading I targeted wasn’t found (looks like the section titles changed during edits). No problem—here’s a **ready-to-paste block** for you to insert just **before** your “Relief Requested” section:

---

### ⬇︎ Paste this into your Rule 70 draft

#### Ground 6 – Operative CMO & disclosure baseline misapprehended  
The PH Order records only the **9 April 2025** specific-disclosure application. However, the Claimant also filed a **trimmed/final Disclosure List on 18 June 2025 (01:07)** expressly **in compliance with the Case Management Order dated 3 June 2025** (served **8 June**). The Written Reasons appear to address disclosure relevance without acknowledging this later, CMO-compliant baseline. The Tribunal is invited to (a) correct the procedural history, and (b) reconsider any relevance assessment that proceeded on the basis of an earlier/obsolete list, so that disclosure directions align with the **3 June CMO** and the **18 June** filing.

*(Evidence: email “Updated Disclosure List – Compliance with CMO dated 3 June 2025 – Case No. 2225465/2024” sent 18 June 2025, 01:07, plus Disclosure List marked “Prepared pursuant to Case Management Orders dated 3 June 2025”.)* fileciteturn58file1 fileciteturn58file2

---

### Also add (if not already) in your **Timeline**:
- **08 Jun 2025** – CMO (dated 3 Jun) **served** by Tribunal.  
- **18 Jun 2025 (01:07)** – Claimant **submits trimmed/final Disclosure List** in **compliance** with the 3 Jun CMO (cover email notes minor delay due to health). fileciteturn58file1

### And append to your **Annexes**:
- **Annex H – 18 Jun 2025 CMO-compliance disclosure (cover email + Disclosure List)** fileciteturn58file1 fileciteturn58file2

---

Want me to try inserting these in the canvas for you? If so, tell me the exact section title where you want “Ground 6” placed (e.g., “## E. Grounds…” or whatever your current heading reads), and I’ll patch it in.

Dear Sir/Madam,

Please find attached my Final Disclosure List, submitted in compliance with the Case Management Order dated 3
June 2025.

I would like to sincerely apologise to the Tribunal and the Respondent for the minor delay in submission. Although
the deadline was today, the document was filed slightly late. This brief delay was caused by a sudden and acute
flare-up of my health condition—specifically, a panic attack—which forms part of my disability discrimination claim.

The pressure of ensuring full compliance with Tribunal directions, combined with ongoing health challenges,
regrettably led to this unintended lapse. I take my obligations to the Tribunal very seriously and have otherwise
taken all steps to comply with orders in full and in good faith.

The Final Disclosure List has now been submitted and simultaneously served on the Respondent.

Yours faithfully, 
Mehmet Bagbozan Claimant

DISCLOSURE LIST FOR TRIBUNAL 
SUBMISSION 

Case No. 2225465/2024 

IN THE LONDON CENTRAL EMPLOYMENT TRIBUNAL 

BETWEEN: 

MR MEHMET BAGBOZAN (Claimant) 

-and- 

THE CO-OPERATIVE GROUP LIMITED (Respondent) 

 

CLAIMANT'S DISCLOSURE LIST 

Prepared pursuant to: Case Management Orders dated 3 June 2025 

Filed by: Mehmet Bagbozan (Claimant in Person) 

Date: 18.06.2025 

 

STATEMENT OF COMPLIANCE 

1. This disclosure list is served in compliance with paragraph 25 of the Case 
Management Orders dated 3 June 2025. 

2. The Claimant has refined this list demonstrating proportionality while preserving 
evidence necessary for fair determination of the issues. 

3. Each request is linked to specific Case Management Order issues and limited to 
named individuals and precise timeframes. 

4. The documents requested are relevant to and necessary for the fair determination 
of the claims as pleaded. 



 

DISCLOSURE REQUESTS 

D1: CCTV Footage - Parcel Incident 

• Documents Required: Complete and unedited CCTV footage from 23 July 2024, 
08:00-18:00, covering the parcel area and all interactions by the Claimant and 
Gaurang Patel, or confirmation that no such footage exists 

• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issues 4.3, 5.3 (comparator analysis for discrimination 
claims) 

• Legal Justification: Direct evidence for testing the Respondent's "theft" 
characterization versus actual facts of the incident 

D2: CCTV Footage - Smoking Areas (ENHANCED) 

• Documents Required: CCTV footage covering designated smoking areas, including 
front entrance areas and any "No Smoking" zones, 26 July - 12 August 2024, 
showing named comparators (Melania Majlat, Layla, Gaurang Patel), or 
confirmation that no such footage exists 

• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issues 4.3, 5.3 (discriminatory enforcement) 
• Legal Justification: Proves selective application of Smoke Free Policy against the 

Claimant; entrance areas specifically prohibited under Co-op policy 
 
 

D3: Internal Communications - Parcel/Smoking Incidents 

• Documents Required: All emails, messages, and internal communications 
between Pankaj Patel, Hasna Ali, and Sanura Dharmasiriwardane regarding the 
parcel and smoking incidents involving the Claimant 

• Timeframe: July-August 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: All issues (intent and bias in disciplinary process) 
• Legal Justification: Evidence of intent and bias in disciplinary action 

D4: Named Comparator Disciplinary Records 

• Documents Required: Complete investigation and disciplinary records, or 
confirmation that no such records exist, for: 



o a. Gaurunbhai Patel: Safe key mishandling incident (Jan-August 2024) 
o b. Melania Majlat, Layla, Gaurunbhai Patel: Smoke Free Policy breaches 

(January-August 2024) 
o c. Melania Majlat, Leila Boufas, Abdullah: Store device removal incidents 

(December 2023-July 2024) 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issues 4.3, 5.3 (less favourable treatment comparison) 
• Legal Justification: Core comparator analysis essential for proving discriminatory 

enforcement under s.13 Equality Act 2010 

D5: Parcel Handling Records 

• Documents Required: All parcel handling logs and internal records for 23-25 July 
2024, or confirmation that no such records exist 

• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issue 1.3 (gross misconduct determination) 
• Legal Justification: Verification of facts underlying the alleged misconduct 

D6: Investigation and Disciplinary Meeting Notes 

• Documents Required: All handwritten and typed meeting notes created by Pankaj 
Patel, Gaurang Patel, and Sanura Dharmasiriwardane 

• Timeframe: 5, 7, 29 July; 12 August 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: All issues (procedural fairness) 
• Legal Justification: Assessment of reliability, impartiality, and procedural 

compliance 

 

D7: Appeal Decision Documentation 

• Documents Required: Complete appeal decision rationale and all internal emails 
relating to the appeal decision 

• Timeframe: August-September 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issue 6 (victimisation) 
• Legal Justification: Evidence supporting victimisation claim and appeal process 

integrity 

D8: Sick Note Communications 

• Documents Required: All communications, emails, messages, and internal 
discussions regarding the Claimant's sick note dated 5 August 2024 



• Timeframe: 1-12 August 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issue 3.1 (knowledge of disability) 
• Legal Justification: Establishing actual knowledge of disability and failure to make 

reasonable adjustments 

D9: Reasonable Adjustments Documentation 

• Documents Required: Any adjustments log, meeting delay decisions, or 
consideration of alternative arrangements, or confirmation that no such 
documentation exists 

• Timeframe: July-August 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issue 3.7 (failure to make reasonable adjustments) 
• Legal Justification: Evidence of procedural failure in disability accommodation 

D10: Performance Management Records 

• Documents Required: All Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) records or 
performance feedback documentation relating to the Claimant, or confirmation 
that no such records exist 

• Timeframe: January-July 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: All claims (proportionality of dismissal) 
• Legal Justification: Assessment of whether dismissal was disproportionate 

response and whether support was provided 

 

D11: Meeting Scheduling During Sick Leave 

• Documents Required: All emails and records confirming the scheduling of 
meetings while the Claimant was on certified sick leave 

• Timeframe: 29 July-12 August 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issue 3.7 (failure to accommodate medical condition) 
• Legal Justification: Evidence of failure to accommodate certified medical unfitness 

D12: Relationship Declarations - Pankaj/Gaurang Patel 

• Documents Required: Any relationship declarations, HR clarifications, or 
documentation regarding the relationship between Pankaj Patel and Gaurang Patel, 
or confirmation that no such documentation exists 

• Timeframe: Any time during their employment 



• Relevance to CMO Issues: All issues (conflict of interest in investigation) 
• Legal Justification: Assessment of conflict of interest undermining investigation 

integrity 

D13: Manager Training Certificates 

• Documents Required: Training completion certificates for Pankaj Patel, Sanura 
Dharmasiriwardane, and Pascal Tokunaga relating to: 

o Disciplinary and Grievance Procedures 
o Equality and Diversity 
o Unconscious Bias training 

• Timeframe: 2022-2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: All issues (procedural competence) 
• Legal Justification: Demonstrates awareness of required standards and ACAS 

Code compliance 

D14: Mental Health and Reasonable Adjustments Policies 

• Documents Required: All policies in force during 1-15 August 2024 governing 
disciplinary proceedings during sickness absence, including: 

o Co-op Well-being Policy 
o Mental Health Adjustment Procedure 
o Stress risk assessment procedures 
o Occupational Health referral protocols for employees on sick leave facing 

disciplinary action 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issue 3 (reasonable adjustments) 
• Legal Justification: Establishes the Respondent's own standards for disability 

accommodation 

D15: Equal Opportunities Policy 

• Documents Required: Equal Opportunities Policy and internal Diversity & Inclusion 
guidance in force during 2022-2024 

• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issues 4.3, 5.3 (discrimination claims) 
• Legal Justification: Relevant to discrimination analysis and comparator treatment 

D16: CCTV Access Authorization Communications 



• Documents Required: All communications regarding CCTV access approval and 
scope of review for the Claimant's incidents 

• Timeframe: 23-26 July 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issues 4.3, 5.3 (selective monitoring) 
• Legal Justification: Transparency of monitoring decisions and evidence of selective 

treatment 

D17: Appeal Meeting Notes 

• Documents Required: Complete appeal meeting notes and summary 
documentation 

• Timeframe: September 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issue 6 (victimisation) 
• Legal Justification: Assessment of appeal process integrity and consideration of 

evidence 

D18: [DELETED] 

D19: Manager Feedback Documentation 

• Documents Required: Any manager feedback, performance notes, or documented 
concerns relating to the Claimant and the disciplinary incidents 

• Timeframe: January 2023-August 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: All claims (evidence of bias) 
• Legal Justification: Contextualizes consistency of treatment and potential bias 

D20: CCTV - Pre-shift Period 8 July 2024 

• Documents Required: CCTV footage for 8 July 2024, 08:30-09:30, shop floor area 
showing Pankaj Patel's interactions, or confirmation that no such footage exists 

• Relevance to CMO Issues: All issues (investigator bias) 
• Legal Justification: Evidence of prejudicial comment ("you're lucky to still have a 

job") demonstrating predetermined attitude 

D21: CCTV - Meeting Rooms 

• Documents Required: CCTV footage of investigation and disciplinary meeting 
rooms during all relevant meetings, or confirmation that no such footage exists 

• Timeframe: 5, 7, 29 July & 12 August 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: Issues 3.1, 3.7 (Claimant's condition during hearings) 



• Legal Justification: Visual evidence of the Claimant's distressed condition and 
procedural conduct 

D22: Staff Rotas 

• Documents Required: Staff duty rotas for investigation and disciplinary meeting 
dates 

• Timeframe: 5, 7, 8, 29 July & 12 August 2024 
• Relevance to CMO Issues: All issues (procedural irregularities) 
• Legal Justification: Evidence of unusual staffing arrangements suggesting 

predetermined approach

parts:
Thanks for the clear steer. I tried to insert your **Grounds 9–13** plus the **extra relief lines** straight into your **Rule 70 main draft** on the canvas, but the update failed because the document’s section headings don’t exactly match what I targeted (the editor couldn’t find “## F. Relief Requested” etc.). Nothing in your doc was changed.

No drama—here’s what I’ll do instead so you have it **now**:

1) I’m giving you the **exact paste blocks** for:
   - **Grounds 9–13** (your wording, lightly polished for consistency).
   - **Additional practical orders invited** (the relief one-liners).

2) If you want me to place them for you, just tell me the **exact text of the heading** that appears **right before your Relief section** (copy/paste that line), and I’ll stitch them in the correct place in one shot.

---

### ✅ Paste block — **Grounds 9–13** (drop these **after your current Ground 8**)

9) **Ground 9 – Adequacy of reasons (Rule 62 / _Meek_ compliance)**  
   The Written Reasons do not grapple with several central points: (i) the **18 June** CMO-compliant disclosure baseline; (ii) the **19 September** PH-bundle omission notice; (iii) the **admission and timing** of the Respondent’s **08:49** same-day skeleton; (iv) the **core RA** (written-as-primary / paced participation) **not being determined**; and (v) **August-adjacent functional evidence** (early-September entries/measures/treatment) which bears on **substantial** effect and **likely to last/likely to recur**. The Claimant invites **supplemental reasons** addressing each point so the parties can understand **what was decided and why**.

10) **Ground 10 – Deposit Order (Rule 40, ET Rules 2024): fairness, affordability, specificity**  
   Any deposit must (a) be **affordable** in light of means; (b) identify **which issues** are said to have **little reasonable prospect** and **why**; and (c) **not** operate as a barrier to justice. The deposit reasons do not explain which allegations are weak and do not show that the Claimant’s **means** were fully weighed. The Claimant invites **reasons** or **variation** of the deposit (including time to pay), particularly in light of the **procedural irregularities** raised in Grounds 6–8.

11) **Ground 11 – Proportionality: strike-out vs alternatives (Rule 3; proper use of r.37)**  
   To the extent the disability limb was treated as having poor prospects, the proportionate course was a **preliminary issue with short medical directions**, not strike-out. Discrimination and victimisation claims are **fact-sensitive** and rarely apt for strike-out; proportionate alternatives (**prelim issue**, **targeted disclosure**, **case-managed timetable**) should be preferred. The Claimant invites reconsideration on a **preliminary-issue** footing rather than striking out or burdening with deposit.

12) **Ground 12 – Material factual misapprehensions affecting discretion**  
   Two factual points appear misstated: (i) the fit-note period is recorded as “a few days”, whereas **MED3s** cover **1–15 Aug** and **15 Aug–1 Sep**; and (ii) victimisation is framed as a **single protected act (appeal)**, whereas earlier communications are relied upon as **protected acts**. These misapprehensions fed into case-management discretion (RA, disclosure scope, deposit). The Claimant invites **correction to the record** and reconsideration on an accurate factual basis.

13) **Ground 13 – Constructive knowledge & duty to adjust (EqA ss.20–21; participation)**  
   By mid-August 2024 the employer had (a) the Claimant’s **MED3s**, (b) **appeal emails** describing **stress/anxiety** and **participation difficulty**, and (c) an **EAP signpost** from management. That combination is capable of founding **knowledge or constructive knowledge** of disability/need for adjustment in the **participation** of internal processes. The reasons do not engage with this knowledge analysis when dismissing adjustments. The Claimant invites reconsideration with findings on **knowledge** and the **PCP** (requirement to attend/participate on 12 Aug without postpone/remote/written/OH).

---

### ✅ Paste block — **Additional practical orders invited**  
Drop these **at the end of your “Relief Requested”** section (or directly under the Relief heading if you prefer):

**Additional practical orders invited:**

Mental Health Statement


Mental Health Impact Statement

Claimant: Mehmet Bagbozan\ Date: 29 July 2025

1. Introduction

My name is Mehmet Bagbozan. I was employed by The Co-operative Group Limited as a Customer Team
Leader from October 2023 until  my dismissal  on 12 August 2024.  This  statement sets out how my
anxiety substantially affects my day-to-day life and meets the definition of a disability under the Equality
Act 2010. The contents of this statement are true to the best of my knowledge and belief.

2. Onset and Diagnosis

My symptoms of anxiety began shortly after starting my role in October 2023. They worsened during
my  probationary  period,  and  by  January  2024  my  difficulties  with  sleep,  concentration,  and  daily
functioning had escalated.

On 1 August 2024, my GP, Dr. Kevin Xu, diagnosed me with "stress at work and anxiety" and issued a
fit note stating I was not fit for work from 1 August 2024 to 1 September 2024.

On 9 September 2024, my GP recorded:  “low mood, poor sleep, might not sleep for a couple of days at
times, irregular appetite, difficult to focus with poor concentration” and that I was “worried generally about
finding another job”.

3. Workplace Causation

The onset and escalation of my anxiety were directly linked to my employment. I began experiencing
symptoms during the three-month probation period, where constant stress and uncertainty about my
role  caused increasing difficulty  with  sleep,  concentration,  and confidence.  By  the extension of  my
probation period in January 2024, my symptoms had significantly worsened, and my health continued
to deteriorate until my eventual dismissal in August 2024.

Specific workplace events contributed to this deterioration. Following the first disciplinary investigation,
I was given a letter stating my job was at risk. Before the disciplinary outcome was even confirmed, my
manager took away my keys and reduced my responsibilities. These measures were not reversed after
the disciplinary outcome. When I returned to the store, my manager said to me,  “the conductor will
decide if you still have a job or not”, and later remarked,  “you’re lucky you still have a job.” These events
intensified my anxiety and reinforced my feelings of instability at work.

These workplace circumstances were the primary cause of the development and aggravation of my
condition.

1



4. Impact on Daily Life

My anxiety has had a significant and ongoing impact on my ability to carry out ordinary daily activities.
Without treatment, the following difficulties occur:

Personal Care: I have been unable to maintain hygiene and clothing organisation. At times, I
struggled to find suitable clean clothes. My GP noted irregular appetite and poor concentration.
Household Tasks: Preparing meals was overwhelming. I often relied on food delivery.
Household organisation became unmanageable.
Sleep: I experienced nights of little or no sleep, sometimes for two consecutive days. This left me
fatigued and unable to function the next day.
Concentration and Memory: I struggled to read, focus, or complete paperwork. My GP
explicitly recorded “difficult to focus with poor concentration”.
Social Interaction: I withdrew from friends and family and isolated myself for long periods. My
family eventually arranged travel for me to Turkey because of concerns about my isolation.
Work-Related Activities: I was unable to sustain confidence in job interviews. In December
2024, Dr. Seah recorded that I experienced “palpitations, unable to speak, mind racing, sometimes
hyperventilates” when attempting interviews. I was also noted as “unable to find employment now”
due to my condition.

5. Treatment and Fluctuation

Therapy (UK): I engaged with Lambeth Talking Therapies from October to November 2024,
attending five sessions of guided self-help CBT with Adelaide Ward. Therapy notes confirm
symptoms of anxiety, rumination, and the need for structured coping strategies.
Medication: On 2 December 2024, I was prescribed Propranolol 40mg daily for anxiety
symptoms.
Therapy (Turkey): From January 2025 I commenced weekly psychotherapy in Turkey, continuing
without interruption since February 2025. My psychiatrist, Prof. Dr. Defne Tamar Gürol, assessed
me in February 2025 as unfit to work and recommended ongoing therapy. My psychologist,
Fundem Ece, confirmed my symptoms were consistent with Generalised Anxiety Disorder.
Current NHS Records (UK): On 14 July 2025, Dr. Xu recorded my return from Turkey and my
request to continue therapy in the UK to avoid losing progress. A referral back to Lambeth
Talking Therapies was made. I have an appointment scheduled for August 2025.

These records demonstrate that my symptoms fluctuate but persist, requiring continuous treatment.

6. Evidence of Long-Term Effect

My symptoms began in January 2024 and remain present in July 2025, approaching two years in
duration.
My GP and therapy records confirm ongoing impairment: poor concentration, disturbed sleep,
irregular appetite, inability to sustain employment.
Objective tests on 9 September 2024 showed: GAD-7: 9/21 (moderate anxiety) and PHQ-9: 12/27
(moderate depression).
I continue to require both medication and weekly psychotherapy. My NHS consultation in July
2025 confirms this ongoing need.
Periods of partial improvement in Turkey show that treatment can reduce symptoms, but relapse
occurred upon my return to the UK, confirming the long-term and fluctuating nature.

2



7. Current Status

I continue to experience difficulties with concentration, communication, sleep, and confidence. I remain
engaged in  weekly  therapy  and  rely  on  ongoing  treatment  to  manage  my  condition.  Without  this
support, I would be unable to leave home, organise daily tasks, or attempt work-related activities.

8. Conclusion

My anxiety has had substantial and long-term adverse effects on my ability to carry out ordinary daily
activities  since  January  2024.  These  effects  include  impairment  of  sleep,  concentration,  social
interaction, personal care, and work-related activities. Despite periods of improvement, my condition
requires continuous management and is likely to continue for 12 months or more.

Statement of Truth

I confirm that the facts stated in this statement are true. I understand that proceedings for contempt of
court  may  be  brought  against  anyone  who  makes,  or  causes  to  be  made,  a  false  statement  in  a
document verified by a Statement of Truth.

Dear Mr Bagbozan,

After your telephone discussion with us an appointment has been made for you to start a course of therapy via
virtual clinics with Adelaide Ward .

Your first session will be on Tuesday 8th October 2024 at 16:15

There are full details with how to set up the virtual clinics on the next page.

Please complete the email questionnaires that you will receive the day before the appointment.

If you are unable to attend please call or email Adelaide Ward . If you do not attend and do not let us know in
advance, with at least 48 hours’ notice, you will not be offered another appointment. If you are late for
your session we might not be able to see you, and this would also count as a missed appointment.

Please note that you are expected to attend your appointment on a weekly basis (at the same time and day) after
your first appointment. Please take some time to read our cancellation policy at the end of this letter. 

If you feel that guided self-help is not the right treatment for you then it would be helpful to discuss this with
your therapist or email LambethIAPTAdministrators@slam.nhs.uk. We have a number of different treatment
options in the service and would be happy to discuss these with you. 

Please read the notes about treatment on the next page and do not hesitate to get in touch with us if you would
like to discuss this further.

If you need to cancel an appointment or have any questions, please contact your therapist directly or email our

Christos Gkasdrogkas

cc:  Lambeth Walk Group Practice, 5 Lambeth Walk, London, Greater London, SE11 6SP



Guidance for virtual clinic appointments

You have been booked in to complete a course of therapy via virtual clinics with Lambeth Talking Therapies.

Each session you and your therapist will log in via Microsoft Teams to have your appointment.

There is no change to the length of therapy sessions or the content covered by having virtual sessions.

Please make sure that you have workable technology (any smart device with a built in camera) to complete these
appointments, and that you can be somewhere private for the duration of the appointment.

You and your therapist will also be able to share documents and homework via the programme.

Instructions for set up

l Check both main inbox and junk mail. If no invitation received please contact your therapist or our main
admin inbox: LambethIAPTAdministrators@slam.nhs.uk

l Please ensure you are in a suitable area where you can complete the session

l A private room where you cannot be over heard or interrupted
l Area with good network coverage

How to prepare for the appointment

l Ensure your device is sufficiently charger i.e. 50% +
l You need any smart device with a built in camera
l May need to download Microsoft Teams App for the first time, in advance of the appointment, this can be
reused for future appointments

l We recommend using headphones for better quality sound

Suitable Network Connections

l Wi-Fi
l Wired Connection
l Mobile Network i.e. 4G, 3G

At the time of appointment, you must ensure you:

l Click on the purple link ‘Join Microsoft Teams’ sent in the email or text
l Click on the ‘Join as Guest’ button when prompted to do so
l Accept permission requests when prompted
l Enable your Camera and Mic with the Teams App
l Where prompted for a name: type in your name (the name known and agreed between you and your
Clinician)

l If name is NOT recognised by the admin/clinician you will not be connected to a clinician
l Clinicians can request for further ID and may ask the following to confirm:

l Full Name
l DOB
l Postcode

If it’s not working

l In the unlikely event that connection is lost wait 1 minute for connection to automatically be re-established
or re-join if prompted.

If after 5 minutes of no connection disconnect and the clinician will call you instead.



Important information about your appointments

First appointment
Your first appointment is for an assessment. At the end, we will discuss with you what help may best meet your
needs. We will inform your GP (or any other professional who referred you) what we have decided to offer, and
the outcome of the treatment.

Urgent help
Please note that we are not an emergency service and are unable to provide immediate support. If you need
urgent help please contact your GP to make an emergency appointment, call the SLaM Mental Health Support
Line (24 hours) on 0800 731 2864 or go to the A and E Department of your local hospital (24hrs).

Other crisis services you can use: Samaritans 24 hour helpline on 116 123 or email jo@samaritans.org, Solidarity
in A Crisis (freephone) on 03001231922, Lambeth Short Term Support Service on 0800 0902456, or The
Listening Place http://listeningplace.org.uk/contact-us/ which is a service run by volunteers supported and
supervised by mental health professionals. 

Our cancellation policy
Missed appointments mean longer waiting times for everyone. Please don’t miss appointments – if you need
to change any appointment then please telephone, send a text message or email us, giving us as much notice as
possible. We will do our best to find a time that suits you but we need your help to make our system work. 
Please always try to keep all your appointments: this will reduce the amount of time other people have to
wait for treatment, and will help you to get the most out of the therapy sessions.  

Cancelled treatment sessions
If you are unable to attend your treatment session, you should contact us as soon as possible, giving at least 48
hours' notice. Please call or email Adelaide Ward or if you cannot get through to them, please contact the admin
team at LambethIAPTAdministrators@slam.nhs.uk so they can inform your clinician. 

For the treatment to work, you need to have regular appointments. If you miss any of your appointments, and do
not call us beforehand to cancel, you may lose that session. Furthermore, if you are late for your session we might
not be able to see you, and this would also count as a missed appointment.  

Treatment sessions not cancelled and not attended without warning

If you do not attend without giving notice, this session might be deducted from the total number of sessions that
will be offered to you.

If you do not attend your session, you will need to contact us within 48 hours of the missed appointment in order
to ensure that your next appointment will take place. If you contact us after this 48hour period then we may still
be able to rebook you, but we will be unable to guarantee you the same appointment time and you may have to
wait. 

If you have to cancel two appointments, you will be discharged and treatment will end. If there are major
unavoidable reasons that stop you coming, please let us know and you may then be able to restart treatment at a
later date when you know you are able to commit to regular attendances. 

Appointments cancelled by us 
We will try hard to offer you good treatment on a regular basis at a convenient time. However sometimes we will
need to alter or cancel an appointment (for example, due to illness). If your therapist needs to cancel an
appointment we will give you as much notice as possible. We will reschedule any sessions cancelled by us: they
will NOT be deducted from the time available for your treatment or reduce the number of sessions available. 

Timekeeping 
It is important that you arrive at your sessions on time. If you are late for a session, you may not be seen. The
session will not be allowed to extend beyond the allotted time frame, therefore any lateness will result in a shorter
session. 

Confidentiality
The information you give is confidential within the NHS. That means it is not disclosed outside of the NHS
unless we have your permission. However, we will inform other people if we think you are at risk to yourself or
to other people. For example if we were concerned that you may be about to harm yourself or another adult or
child. Then we would be required to inform other authorities.

Questionnaires
Your therapist will ask you to complete questionnaires about how you are feeling and doing, every week. This is



essential so that we can keep track of your progress. They will also ask you to do other tasks in your week,
including completing diaries for homework. This is to make sure that what we do works in your everyday life.

Research opportunity
If you are interested in taking part in research, Lambeth Talking Therapies is collaborating with the Genetic
Links to Anxiety and Depression (GLAD) Study. This would allow you to take part in research studies about
psychological wellbeing and talking therapies. The goal is to better understand anxiety and depression and to
improve treatment for anyone who has experienced these difficulties. For more information, see the attached
leaflet or visit www.gladstudy.org.uk.

http://www.gladstudy.org.uk/


 
What is Guided Self-Help?

Guided self-help is a form of therapy involving self-help materials based on Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy (CBT). 
You will be supported by a Psychological Wellbeing Practitioner to learn techniques to help manage symptoms of 
depression, anxiety, panic attacks, phobias and stress. You will be asked to do some in-between session tasks and the
emphasis will be on providing you with techniques and coping strategies that you can use independently in the long
term. 

What happens in Guided Self-Help sessions?

The sessions are offered weekly, typically up to 6 sessions.  Each treatment session will last up to 30 minutes;
therefore sessions will be focused and structured in order for you to get the most out of your treatment. Guided
self-help is a collaborative treatment, so together in each session, you and a Psychological Wellbeing Practitioner will
aim to:

l Set an agenda for the session
l Identify your priorities and goals for the session
l Work through a range of guided self-help booklets
l Guide you in how to use the guided self-help techniques and apply them to your daily life
l Set in-between session tasks to help you practice the techniques
l Review how you get on with in-between session tasks

What are in-between session tasks and why are they important?

In-between session (or ‘homework’) tasks are set at the end of each session and are a key method of change in guided
self-help. As the sessions are only 30 minutes long, most of the practical work will be done outside of sessions. This
enables you to try out the techniques in your everyday life and test out how well they work for you.

It is important to complete the in-between session tasks because many of the techniques will be new and will need to
be developed through repeated practice. Regular practice of the techniques is essential in order for change to come
about and for you to see improvements in symptoms of depression and anxiety.

How is Guided self-help delivered?

Guided self-help can be done individually or with a group of people. It can also be done using self-help materials or
an online computer programme.  It can be delivered in person, over the phone or virtually.

How effective is Guided self-help?

Guided self-help is the first-line intervention recommended by the NICE guidelines for a range of anxiety disorders
and depression.  It is most effective when sessions are attended regularly and when in-between sessions tasks are
completed.

Good Thinking

Good Thinking is a digital wellbeing site that includes information, advice, quizzes, self-assessments and links to
helpful apps and tools to help manage a variety of different conditions such as sleep issues, stress, anxiety and low
mood. Their website provides a variety of interesting, helpful and free podcasts, videos, webinars and blogs that aim
to promote positive mental wellbeing. This is an excellent resource to use while you wait for treatment, during
treatment, or to even keep learning CBT skills after treatment has finished to aid recovery.

ACE ACTIVITY 

Aim for a healthy life balance:  Achieve, Connect, Enjoy 

Our mood can be greatly affected by what we do, when, and with whom.  

In order to maintain a healthy sense of wellbeing, we need 
to balance what we do.  We can use the acronym ACE to 

help us remember: 

 ACHIEVE - work, chores, study 

 CONNECT -  with friends, family, community 

 ENJOY – play, fun, pleasure 

When we feel stressed, we often spend more time doing 

things that help us achieve, but less of enjoyment and 

connecting with others.   When we feel depressed, we 

withdraw and isolate ourselves and do much less, and 

when we feel anxious, we tend to avoid places or people 

where we feel anxious. 

Make time for yourself each day - relaxation, fun, enjoyment. Create a healthy balance 

- allow time for activities which give you a sense of achievement, those that give a 

sense of connecting with and of being close to others, and of a sense of enjoyment.  

These activities affect our brain chemistry by acting directly on the release of neuro-

transmitters, and are our natural anti-stress and anti-depressants. 

 Achievement stimulates dopamine 
 Purposeful activity stimulates serotonin 

 Connecting with other people stimulates oxytocin  

 Exercise stimulates endorphins 

Therefore, making sure we keep doing these ACE activities every day, will help us 

overcome our problems.

- **Pleadings line quoted:** They expressly say (in terms) *“the Claimant has failed to set out the PCP, why it put him at a disadvantage, and what adjustments should have been made… the head should be struck out”* (with page refs within their bundle).

# Why the **08:49 service** is procedurally significant
- **Timing:** Served **~1 hour before** a **10:00** PH; the covering email asks that it be *“placed before the Employment Judge… for use at the hearing today”*.  
- **Fairness context:** You had a **live participation RA** (written-as-primary, paced participation) that **was not determined** in advance. Admitting a fresh skeleton at 08:49 **changed the terrain** of the hearing (introducing a strike-out ask on RA pleadings) without giving you a reasonable chance to **prepare, respond in writing, or amend**.  
- **Practical prejudice:**  
  - You could not produce a **written reply** or a **brief amendment** to crystallise PCP/disadvantage/adjustments (which is the orthodox cure where pleading particularity is in issue).  
  - You were required to **answer orally**, despite anxiety and the absence of a written-first accommodation.

# What this means in **Rule-70** terms (your strongest angle)
1) **Rule 3 / Rule 38(2) breach (equal footing / reasonable opportunity):**

2) **Proportionality error:**
